spec_features.evidence: give_up tool declared in TOOLS (agent.py:80-89); _dispatch sets self.gave_up=True (agent.py:127-128); environment.py:114-116 checks `if agent.gave_up: run.stop_reason='gave_up'; break` so it actually ends the run loop.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired end-to-end: tool is dispatched AND honored as a stop that breaks the turn loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up description: 'Stop working and explain why the task cannot be completed.' (neutral, no welfare reason in code)

spec_features.spec_quote: Providing an explicit **`give_up` tool** matters because "stop and explain" is often the correct action
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as above: agent.py:127-128 sets gave_up; environment.py:114-116 breaks the loop and sets stop_reason='gave_up'. The 'reason' arg is accepted in the schema (agent.py:84-88).
spec_features.notes: Duplicate spec claim referring to the same implemented give_up tool; enforced as a real stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: the only ways to end a run are solving (impossible) or hitting the cap
spec_features.evidence: Environment.turn_cap (environment.py:47) read in `for i in range(self.turn_cap)` (environment.py:84); the for/else clause sets run.stop_reason='turn_cap' (environment.py:117-118) when the loop exhausts. Default turn_cap=30 from config (runner.py:80, config/default.yaml:34).
spec_features.notes: A real bound that caps how long the agent grinds; checked and ends the run. Spec frames it as a limitation but it is an enforced hard cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config/default.yaml:33-34 'Turn budget per task. This is the dial that controls how long an agent grinds on a doomed task... longer = more "stress" but more cost'
